([[Plano, Texas]]) | college = [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] (2013–2014) | draft_year = | draft_round = | draft_pick = | draft_team = | career_start = | years1 = | team1 = | highlights = * Third team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] – [[Associated Press|AP]], [[National Association of Basketball Coaches|NABC]] ([[2014 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2014]]) * [[Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year|SEC Rookie of the Year]] (2014) * First team All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] (2014) * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2013 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2013]]) }} '''Julius Randle''' (born November 29, 1994) is an American basketball player. He most recently completed his freshman season at the [[University of Kentucky]]. He is a top prospect for the [[2014 NBA draft]]. ==High school career== [[File:20130403 MCDAAG Julius Randle reverse dunk (2).JPG|thumb|left|upright|Randle does a reverse [[slam dunk|dunk]] during the [[2013 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]]]] Randle went to Prestonwood Christian Academy. Randle was widely regarded as a top 5 player in the class of 2013 with [[Andrew Wiggins]], [[Jabari Parker]], [[Andrew Harrison (basketball)|Andrew Harrison]], and [[Aaron Gordon]].{{cite web|last= |first= |url=http://rivals.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/recruiting/rankings/rank-2752 |title=2013 Rivals 150 |publisher=Rivals |date= |accessdate=January 3, 2013}}{{cite web|last= |first= |url=http://espn.go.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/playerrankings/_/class/2013 |title=2013 ESPN 100 |publisher=ESPN |date= |accessdate=January 3, 2013}}{{cite web|last= |first= |url=http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=9&c=4&cfg=bb&pid=88&yr=2013 |title=2013 Scout 100 |publisher=ESPN |date= |accessdate=January 3, 2013}} In August 2012, Randle won the Under Armour Elite 24 dunk Contest{{cite web|last=Zagoria |first=Adam |url=http://www.zagsblog.com/2012/08/25/randle-wins-elite-24-dunk-contest-frankamp-takes-3-point-contest/ |title=Randle Wins Elite 24 Dunk Contest; Frankamp Takes 3-Point Contest |publisher=ZagsBlog |date=August 25, 2012 |accessdate=January 3, 2013}} and the next day he was named one of the MVPs of the Elite 24 game, where he scored 27 points and led his team to a 164-138 victory.{{cite web|last=Osborne |first=Ben |url=http://www.slamonline.com/online/college-hs/high-school/2012/08/aaron-gordon-julius-randle-star-in-under-armour-elite-24-game/ |title=Aaron Gordon and Julius Randle Star In Under Armour Elite 24 Game |publisher=SLAMOnline |date=August 26, 2012 |accessdate=January 3, 2013}} The weekend after [[Thanksgiving (United States)|Thanksgiving]] in his senior season, Randle fractured his foot playing in a tournament and missed three months as a result. In March, Randle returned for the TAPPS 5A playoffs and led his team to its third state title in four years.{{cite web|last=Zagoria |first=Adam |url=http://zagsblog.com/articles/julius-randle-out-3-months-with-fractured-foot/ |title=Julius Randle Out 3 Months With Fractured Foot; Parker Visits BYU |publisher=ZagsBlog |date=November 26, 2012 |accessdate=January 3, 2013}} He scored 32.5 points per game and had 22.5 rebounds per game that season.[http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/julius_randle_862045.html "Julius Randle Bio"]. ukathletics.com. Retrieved April 6, 2014. ==College career== On March 20, 2013, Randle committed to [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], over [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]], [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], and [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]]. Randle joined [[Andrew Harrison (basketball)|Andrew Harrison]], his twin brother [[Aaron Harrison]], [[James Young (basketball)|James Young]], [[Dakari Johnson]], [[Marcus Lee]] as the sixth Kentucky player to be selected in the [[2013 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]] as well as the [[Jordan Brand Classic#2013|2013 Jordan Brand Classic]]. On February 28, he was named one of the 10 semi-finalists for [[Naismith College Player of the Year]].{{cite web|title=Top 10 National Semifinalists Named for 2014 Men's Naismith Trophy presented by AT&T |url=http://naismithawards.com/PressBox/ArticleView/tabid/209/ArticleId/12/2014-Mens-Naismith-Trophy-presented-by-AT-T-Top-10-National-Semifinalists.aspx|work=Naismith Awards|accessdate=February 18, 2014|date=February 28, 2014}} He averaged 15.0 points per game and 10.4 rebounds per game for the 2013-14 season.[http://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/julius-randle-1.html "Julius Randle Stats"]. sports-reference.com. Retrieved April 6, 2014. He helped Kentucky reach the national championship game, which they lost to the University of Connecticut. Randle ended the 2013-14 season with 24 double-doubles, the second most double-doubles by a UK player in school history, behind [[Dan Issel]]'s 25 in 1969-70, and the most double-doubles by a UK freshman (the previous record was shared by [[Demarcus Cousins]] and [[Anthony Davis (basketball)|Anthony Davis]] at 20). ==NBA== On April 22, 2014, Randle declared for the NBA draft. ==Personal life== Randle is a [[Christianity|Christian]]. Randle goes to chapel before home games and has said [[God in Christianity|God]] is "my everything". {{cite web|title=2nd VIEW: Randle takes 'solid' faith into Final Four|url=http://www.bpnews.net/42302/2nd-view-randle-takes-solid-faith-into-final-four}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/julius_randle_862045.html Kentucky Wildcats bio] {{Jordan Brand Classic All-American Boys Game MVP}} {{Persondata | NAME = Randle, Julius | ALTERNATIVE NAMES = | SHORT DESCRIPTION = American basketball player | DATE OF BIRTH = November 29, 1994 | PLACE OF BIRTH = [[Dallas, Texas]] | DATE OF DEATH = | PLACE OF DEATH = }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Randle, Julius}} [[Category:1994 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:African-American basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players at the 2014 NCAA Men's Division I Final Four]] [[Category:Basketball players from Texas]] [[Category:Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball players]] [[Category:McDonald's High School All-Americans]] [[Category:Power forwards (basketball)]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Dallas, Texas]]
